title: Size the sample to the claim
statement: Claim a rate or a difference only from a sample sized to show it, with the count reported, and a difference only once it clears the judge's run-to-run spread.
example: On 15-item runs the noise floor was roughly ±1 row per type, so a split of 2/3 against 0/3 was read as directional only.
detail: AP lab analyses kept asking whether a sample could carry the claim made from it. One report called n=45 per type small for a 95 % gate, with one type alone at 25 misses; another put the noise floor of 15-item runs at roughly ±1 row per type and read splits like 2/3 against 0/3 as directional only; and a handoff rule calls any expected lift under 1.0 point below the noise floor for n=150 measurements. A test needs enough items of each type to tell a high gate from a lower rate. The noise to clear is about twice the judge's spread on unchanged items, and a small-sample win is confirmed on more items.
against: The project kept deciding on small samples: a winner was declared on 10 items ("| **Two-Stage Generation** | **100%** (10/10) | ✅ WINNER |", `icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/docs/archive/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS_2026-02-18.md`, line 15), and its blueprint kept a 12-question check for iteration (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/docs/archive/RUN7_BLUEPRINT.md`, line 1006). The 12-item check did not evaluate cognitive demand (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/docs/archive/RUN6_ANALYSIS.md`, line 14), so its 100% reflects a missing criterion as well as sample size. Where the judge is deterministic, any difference counts (`project_grader_variance_discovered.md`, line 42), and re-scoring stored outputs measures only the judge, while fresh generation adds noise of its own (`feedback_baseline_must_be_fresh_gen.md`, line 49). Doubt about a small sample scales with a type's history: types that had held at 95-100% for several versions were more credible at 100 items (`feedback_n_scale_tightens_CI_exposes_n100_anomalies_2026_06_01.md`, line 26). A swing from 20 of 20 to 0 of 100 is too large for sampling error alone, so those runs probably differed in more than size. Most of the document-based spread was later traced to the pass/fail cut ('DBQ "noise" was ~all threshold artifact', `icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/MEMORY.md`, line 113), and a long-essay type was one of the two that did not vary, so the spread is not simply a matter of length. The spreads come from three runs on one set of saved outputs, so the thresholds are rough: "**Finding (T0, 3 independent IB v2.5.3 runs on identical v29 gens, 2026-04-29):**" (icloud-work/aptraining/workspace/comms/from_shadow/2026-04-30T1700Z_comprehensive_lessons_learned.md, 132). Where the spread is zero, any change counts: "- MCQ/LEQ: essentially deterministic (σ=0), any non-zero delta is real" (the same file, 144). Small gains need many items: at 30 items per type a paired test detects differences of about 0.05 or more with 80% power, and smaller ones need 120 or more per type (`icloud-work/aptraining/handover/2026-05-01T1039Z_compass_session_close/03_R41D_implementation.md`). A continuous score also needs a freshly generated baseline, without which several regressions reversed (`icloud-work/aptraining/handover/2026-05-01T1039Z_main_session_close/02_CONSOLIDATED_STATE.md`). And an aggregate can look steady while item types swing: across three seeds the overall rate had a standard deviation under a point while one type passed 6, 7 and 9 of 30 (`icloud-work/aptraining-crystal-copy-20260521/full-copy/aptraining-root/achieved.md`). The generator changed between runs, so the swings mix real change with sampling noise, and cells this small cannot separate the two. A mechanical count rule misfires when the small number is a breakdown rather than the support, as with the report it rejected: "the document's verdict is supported by aggregate n=30 (30/30 v40h fabrications + 30/30 v29 fabrications); the n=6 is per-cell stratification (a methodological detail, not the support). R1 doesn't distinguish "support n" from "incidental n."" (icloud-work/aptraining/workspace/comms/_deprecated/outboxes/from_oracle/2026-05-04T1713Z_validator_findings.md, 88) The writer changed between runs, so the reversals mix changes to the writer with sampling noise, and no two runs repeat the same writer and judge (`icloud-work/evaluator/docs/reports/BENCHMARK_RUN4_REPORT.md`). The same project still read a one-item difference on a 30-item set as a win: a change that moved one course's items from 86.7% to 90% was recorded as the first evidence that the method worked (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/research/OVERNIGHT_RECAP.md`; `icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/BEADS.md`).
